question: Does the sole locally converged HORM E-F-H candidate from native-construction shard 3 connect two distinct HORM minima under full-Hessian IRC validation?
hypothesis: A locally index-one, low-force candidate is usable only if both downhill branches relax to distinct endpoint minima.
design: Run the existing full-Hessian IRC and endpoint-relaxation validator on candidate_000_sample_0080.npz from shard 3 using the conservative HORM LEFTNet E-F-H checkpoint.
decision_rule: Use it in a matched GAD/Sella comparison only if both endpoints are converged, distinct, and the candidate is index one. Otherwise mark it invalid for optimizer benchmarking.

resources.allocation: def-aspuru: one A100 3g.20gb MIG slice, 4 CPU cores, 20G memory, 60 minutes

result: candidate_000_sample_0080.npz is locally converged and index one, but both full-Hessian IRC branches relax to the reactant-side minimum (endpoint minima true; intended connectivity false). It is invalid for an intended-saddle optimizer benchmark.
next_action: Do not use this candidate for GAD/Sella rates; retain it only as a stationarity-versus-connectivity diagnostic.
